payload.label: Size of a yeast population grown in a closed flask

stimuli.alt_text: Yeast population over 24 hours: 2, 6, 18, 40, 58, 62, 63 million cells at 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24 hours.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Construct a graph of yeast population size versus time using the data provided. Label and scale both axes and plot the data appropriately.

criteria.description: Both axes labeled with quantity and units and scaled appropriately, with time on the x-axis and population on the y-axis.
All seven data points plotted accurately.
Uses an appropriate representation (line or smooth curve connecting the trend) for continuous growth data.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Describe the pattern of population growth shown by the data.

criteria.description: Identifies an early phase of rapid, roughly exponential increase.
Identifies later leveling off toward a maximum (approaching carrying capacity).
Supports the description with reference to the data (e.g., near-constant ~62-63 million after 20 hours).

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Identify one factor that could be responsible for the population leveling off in the closed flask, and explain how it limits growth.

criteria.description: Identifies a plausible density-dependent limiting factor (e.g., nutrient depletion, accumulation of waste/ethanol, limited space).
Explains how that factor reduces the per-capita growth rate as the population grows.

accessibility.accommodation_notes: Part (a) requires a constructed graph (graph modality) — a non-text response that needs an accessible construction/alternative path; the source data is provided as a table with alt_text so the prompt is readable without the graph.
